note: Results registry (PC1). One entry per result shown on the site (science.html renders it). Owners fill 'summary' (one plain sentence, no hype) and 'key_number' (with unit and quality tag) from their own data files; numbers must match PC5/PC4 numbers registry.
quality_note: NISAR data are provisional. Calibration and validation are carried out by the NISAR project (NASA-JPL and ISRO), not by our team.

items.title: Independent check of the atlas top ranks
items.summary: Every headline value is checked against its own time series; steps of one full L-band phase cycle (12.1 cm) or a single bad acquisition move a region to indicative only.

items.title: Where the ground is sinking fastest in 2026
items.summary: Across 29 regions in the 2026 Global Subsidence Atlas (16 reliable, 13 indicative), Konya Plain leads reliable basins at -11.0 cm/100d over the 93-day common window (-9.6 cm LOS, low-coverage caution), followed by Eloy, Central Valley, Kashmar, and Mashhad.

items.title: Literature and first-measurement audit
items.summary: Literature audit excludes individual first-with-NISAR claims for Mexico City (already published by NASA-JPL) and checks peer-reviewed InSAR/GNSS rates across atlas basins using provisional GUNW data.

items.title: Detectability and minimum detectable rate
items.summary: All 12 audited summer basins exceed 2-sigma formal radar phase-noise thresholds (0.544-0.615 cm/100d, SNR 3.7-28.9), while UK London Clay sets an empirical scene-level 3-sigma atmospheric floor of 3.62 cm.

items.title: Ranking robustness: reference, coherence and box variants
items.summary: Reference and spatial box variants across 17 global cities show rank stability under alternative unwrapping baselines.

items.title: NISAR vs NASA JPL OPERA DISP-S1 cross-check
items.summary: Against non-overlapping NASA OPERA DISP-S1 frames, NISAR correlates strongly in steady clay-compaction Mexico City (r = 0.912, n = 10) and moderately in same-season Central Valley (r = 0.399, n = 7,571), while seasonal spring-vs-summer mismatch and 80.6% C-band masking explain Eloy (r = 0.091, n = 581).

items.title: People and crops on sinking ground
items.summary: Across 21 measured atlas regions, 549.45 km2 sinks faster than -5 cm per 108 days, affecting 1,479,844 residents (8,251,911 below -2 cm/108d, excluding nested Karapinar).

items.title: Full year: winter rebound vs permanent compaction
items.summary: Over 324 days (2025-11-24 to 2026-10-14, 25 mixed beta-precal + provisional pairs), peak cumulative LOS subsidence at Earlimart reaches -20.3 cm (-26.9 cm vertical est.; 3-reference range -20.3 to -11.7 cm). Harmonic decomposition separates a valley median permanent rate of -3.74 cm/yr (-16.77 cm/yr at Earlimart p01) from 5.83 cm seasonal amplitude.
items.key_number: -16.77 cm/yr permanent at Earlimart (-20.3 cm 324-d LOS, mixed)

items.title: Permanent aquifer storage loss (O1)
items.summary: Integrating permanent vertical compaction across 4,508.29 km2 in the Tulare Basin yields 0.317 km3/yr permanent aquifer storage loss (3-reference range 0.066-0.320 km3/yr).

items.title: Probabilistic engineering risk for canals and roads (O2)
items.summary: Monte Carlo analysis of 2,082 Central Valley infrastructure segments evaluating angular distortion beta and differential settlement exceedance.

items.title: GNSS validation
items.summary: Across 10 Nevada Geodetic Laboratory GPS stations in the San Joaquin Valley, 6 stations agree with NISAR vertical estimates (r >= 0.4, median RMSE 0.8 cm; all-10 median RMSE 1.0 cm, peak CAHA r = 0.90).

items.title: L-band NISAR vs C-band Sentinel-1
items.summary: In California's Tulare Basin, L-band NISAR retains 80%-93% usable phase over irrigated crops (10-GPS r = 0.924, 5-core RMSE = 0.82 cm) and matches published C-band trends (-16.8 +/- 2.2 cm/yr vs -17.7 to -34.5 cm/yr).

items.title: Groundwater and crop drivers
items.summary: Across N = 8 summer epochs in Central Valley, preliminary soil-moisture and irrigation-index correlations (r = 0.573-0.654) remain statistically non-significant (p = 0.08-0.16 vs |r_crit| = 0.707-0.754).

items.title: Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta levees
items.summary: Over the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta (2026-06-17 to 2026-10-15, 10 provisional pairs), 1-km block peak LOS subsidence is -1.3 cm (2-reference range -1.3 to -1.1 cm).

items.title: Konya Closed Basin: Konya, Çumra and Karapınar
items.summary: Across the Konya Plain (2026-06-26 to 2026-10-12, 8 provisional pairs), 1-km block peak LOS subsidence reaches -9.6 cm (3-reference range -14.0 to -9.6 cm) and is confirmed by ascending Path 172.

items.title: Karapınar sinkholes and subsidence: statistical test
items.summary: Around 29 verified Karapınar sinkholes, 1.04 km block permutations (p = 0.0001) and 3,423 rigid constellation shifts (p = 0.0207) show -3.04 to -3.41 cm deeper LOS subsidence within 0-2 km.

items.title: London Clay detection limit and Holme Fen
items.summary: Over Greater London (21 Jun-19 Oct 2026, 9 pairs), 1-km block atmospheric noise (3-sigma = 3.62 cm) exceeds expected 0.5-2.0 cm seasonal clay motion, leaving zero detected blocks.

items.title: Which polarization shows crop-stage change (Fens)
items.summary: Comparison of HH, HV, and cross-ratio backscatter in the Fens shows HV cross-polarization is the most interpretable channel for canopy volume scattering.

items.title: NISAR Pulse: one-command open engine (O3)
items.summary: NISAR Pulse automates CMR search, 20-MB subsetting, pixel-level cycle-jump and single-date QC (--qc), quality metrics, and coverage reporting from a single --center lon,lat command.

items.title: Uncertainty budget
items.summary: Over 7 provisional Central Valley pairs (108 d), local phase-noise RMS averages 0.66 cm/pair (1.7 cm local to 2.9 cm scene-wide cumulative), placing the -7.8 cm LOS peak 2.7x-4.5x above noise.

items.title: Calibration status of the NISAR products we used
items.summary: NISAR data are provisional (product code P05023 from 2026-06-17; validated status from 2026-10-21); calibration and validation are carried out by the NISAR project (NASA-JPL and ISRO), not by our team.

items.title: Technical note (NASA report style)
items.summary: Methods, uncertainty limits, GNSS/OPERA cross-checks, and 29-region ATLAS v2 results for provisional NISAR L-band GUNW interferometry across Central Valley, Konya Basin, UK Fens, and global subsidence basins.

items.title: Global subsidence atlas (common-window ranked)
items.summary: 29 sinking regions ranked over a common 93-day summer window (2026-06-28 to 2026-09-29) using provisional NISAR GUNW chains.
items.key_number: 29 regions (16 reliable, 13 indicative); top reliable -11.0 cm/100d (Konya Plain)

items.title: Global atlas transparent changelog
items.summary: Machine-readable log of every region addition, QC flag, confidence change, and headline correction (>0.5 cm) across atlas builds.

items.title: Independent literature & QC audit (ranks 6–16)
items.summary: Step-by-step p01 time-series QC and peer-reviewed literature comparison across reliable ranks 6–16 (Mexico City to Quetta); 9 consistent, 2 caution (Houston, Quetta), 0 suspect.

items.title: Published InSAR & GNSS literature rates (29 basins)
items.summary: Aggregated peer-reviewed vertical subsidence rates with verified DOIs and agreement notes alongside common 93-day and full-window NISAR L-band rates.

items.title: Valley Under Pressure: 24-month aquifer simulator
items.summary: Interactive browser simulator calibrated to Terra Bella 1970–2026 compaction and Karapınar NISAR rates, linking pumping decisions to permanent clay compaction and canal tilt.

items.title: Offline 6-stop Lincoln presentation deck
items.summary: Keyboard-navigable full-screen walkthrough (Home, 29-region Atlas, Konya Plain, Semarang QC catch, GNSS/tilt validation, Simulator) working offline from local assets.

items.title: NASA Space Apps 2026 submission package
items.summary: Complete Space Apps delivery checklist, HTTP-200 verified live URLs, NASA/ESA/JRC data inventory, and AI usage disclosure.
